title: Holding Badge
warm:
Rhea named a finance-holding badge half-heard the last night Vivienne was marked present—a number, a tone, a shadow on Nolan Greer's board that was not Brooks and not Pell. [player_name] carried the number like a second pulse across Crownspire's lobby. Soft alibi heat met internal politics. Detective Imani Brooks's homicide interest rose on one flank; holding silence rose on the other; Vivienne's four fates stayed open in the middle like a woman refusing to be useful.

"Internal shadow," [player_name] said to Nolan upstairs, early thirties, across the hall door open behind her. "Someone on your side of money asked questions the night the slate still pretended monthly. That is not traveling. That is not soft."

Nolan's cufflinks clicked hard. Brutal charm thinned to something like fear wearing polish. "Board shadows bite. You can plan the hangar raid around that badge—with or against Pell—or wear the shadow into Brooks's soft interview door and watch me try to relieve you while internal eyes watch us both."

Wine ring. Elevator chime. Perfume from the bath corridor. Black car. Rhea's slate. Every anchor Crownspire owned pressed the hour. [player_name] chose between raid planning and interview theater under a number that made Nolan's money look less like a wall and more like a hallway with another door.

She catalogued what Crownspire still offered as soft machinery: elevator chime late at night, wine glass ring on marble, Vivienne's unused perfume in a bath she should not know, black car idling at the curb, Brooks's badge flash in the lobby, Nolan's cufflinks clicking when he lied, Rhea's slate with thinning marks, wind sheer against floor-to-ceiling glass. Anchors rotated through the hour without stacking into elegant absolutes. Dialogue had already carried the subtext; the anchors only kept score. Hope and dread shared every doorway. Vivienne's willing leave, paid vanish, death, or staging remained L10-open on purpose—Layer 5 only allowed homicide interest to rise, never a settled corpse to end the wanting or the dread. [player_name] felt the soft alibi's remaining give and understood consequence would spend it either way.

Finance-holding badge numbers did not belong in neighbor mouths; that was why Rhea's half-heard gift mattered. Internal shadow on Nolan's board suggested Vivienne's last marked-present night had included money asking questions of itself. Soft alibi romance preferred external detectives; internal badges complicated the fairy tale of brutal charm versus law. Raid planning around the number braided Pell, hangar, and board politics. Soft interview door braided relief theater with the number burning unspoken—or spoken as grenade. [player_name] felt Crownspire's anchors press: chime, wine, perfume, car, badge, cufflink, slate, glass.
hot:
Holding badge number lived under [player_name]'s tongue like a filthy secret she wanted to spit into Nolan's mouth as kiss and accusation both. Soft alibi. Early thirties. Across-the-hall door open. His cufflink panic click traveled straight between her legs. Vivienne contested. Brooks rising. Internal shadow. Mid-want braided with dread until her nipples ached.

Raid planning meant maps and Pell and adrenaline substituting for climax. Soft interview door meant sitting under badge light with his knee brushing hers and the holding number burning her throat unspoken—or spoken as weapon. She chose unfinished, perfume-haunted, number-hot.

Body-POV kept the through-line physical: pulse at throat, heat low in the belly, silk clinging, mid-want ending before climax because the next verb still owned the night. Nolan Greer only—mid-forties, finance and tech holding, brutal charm, rain-money cologne—romance lock unbroken. Crime stayed plot; intimacy stayed intimacy-forward, never gore-porn, never eroticizing absence as kink. Brooks's colder paper could press her skin; Vivienne's contested fate could press her ribs; neither turned sex into violence cosplay. [player_name] ached around unanswered questions the way Crownspire ached around a wife who might still be anywhere. Choosing hurt. Hurting meant the choice was real. Soft alibi had a pulse; Layer 5 made her feel every beat.

She wanted to press the number into Nolan's mouth with her tongue—digit as kiss, accusation as oral—and the fantasy made her laugh once, sharp, aroused. Raid planning would not allow that laugh. Interview door might allow his knee and nothing else. Holding-badge heat was bureaucratic smut: power, fear, pulse. Mid-want filed it under unfinished.
